messages:
customer-corp: Hey, hitting intermittent 504s and EOFs from the Go SDK in our prod service since last deploy. Happens under load surge (~200rps) and manifests as retries piling up. SDK version v0.9.3. Logs show a bunch of 'read tcp ...: connection reset by peer' and 'http2: client conn not available' entries. Any quick ideas?
eli: Sorry about that — can you paste a short snippet of how you're creating the http client / context + the SDK call? Also which Go runtime version?
customer-corp: Sure — using default client mostly, with a custom transport: ```go tr := &http.Transport{ForceAttemptHTTP2: true, MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 200, IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second} client := &http.Client{Transport: tr, Timeout: 15 * time.Second} ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second) defer cancel() resp, err := sdk.Client.Call(ctx, req) ``` Go 1.18. We cancel ctx after 10s which sometimes races with retries.
mika: Two quick suspects: (1) Go 1.18 had a couple http2 connection reuse edge cases when requests are cancelled — connections could get into a bad state and then next request fails with EOF/reset. (2) SDK retry loop + context cancellation might not be closing the request body in all branches, leaving the Transport confused.
devin: Can you reproduce locally with a short harness? If so, run with GODEBUG=http2debug=1 and capture logs, or tcpdump to see RST bursts. Also try ForceAttemptHTTP2=false as an experiment. If the failures disappear, it's likely an http2 reuse issue.
customer-corp: Quick test: set ForceAttemptHTTP2:false and reduced MaxIdleConnsPerHost to 50. Re-ran for 5 min under the same load — still saw a couple 504s but far fewer EOFs.
eli: Good repro. Two mitigation paths: (A) short-term: disable HTTP/2 or set Transport.DisableKeepAlives=true so connections are not reused (higher CPU but more stable), and bump client Timeout > per-request expected time so ctx cancels less often. (B) longer term: upgrade to Go 1.20+ where several http2 fixes landed, and we should release SDK v0.9.4 that ensures request bodies are closed on cancel and uses a better retry backoff that avoids tight bursts.
customer-corp: Any suggested SDK config we can change now without code changes in our service? We can't re-deploy app yet.
mika: If you can control env, set GODEBUG=http2debug=1 to gather evidence. You can also patch the outbound proxy (if you have one) to limit concurrent streams per connection as a hack. Otherwise, throttling request rates from the caller side or adding a small jitter before automatic retries helps.
devin: We're going to push a hotfix for the SDK retry loop to master that ensures the SDK doesn't retry on ctx.Err() and always closes the request body. I'll post a PR and a patched release candidate. For now: try ForceAttemptHTTP2=false via the SDK config override if available, or set HTTP transport options via the Go http client passed into the SDK.
customer-corp: Thanks — attaching a small log excerpt: ```
2026-03-15T18:22:11Z ERROR: transport: read tcp 10.1.1.4:56748->13.224.45.6:443: read: connection reset by peer
2026-03-15T18:22:11Z WARN: http2: client conn not available
2026-03-15T18:22:11Z ERROR: sdk/retries: attempt 3: context canceled
```
eli: Looks consistent. I'll follow up with the PR link and an SDK rc in this thread. deploy-bot: build/rc v0.9.4-rc1 created for branch fix/retry-cancel-closure :white_check_mark:
customer-corp: Awesome — will try rc1 in a staging slot and report back. Appreciate the fast turnaround :thumbsup:
eli: Thanks for testing — keep us posted and if you can include a small tcpdump or http2 debug log we can be confident this is the same issue across customers.
